title: obs-pipeline-logtrace-scratchpad
content:
Personal scratchpad for the log/tracing ingestion issue affecting staging -> prod parity. Raw dump of commands, partial outputs, and hypotheses so I don't forget half the things I tried at 2am.

Summary:
- Symptoms: sudden drop in service trace counts (Jaeger spans) and intermittent "metrics series dropped" alerts for several services (service-A, service-batch-ingest). Logs for some pods (ingest-fluentbit) show JSON parse failures. Prometheus scrape count stable but series cardinality decreased for a few key latency metrics.
- First noticed: 2025-02-02 22:30 UTC when QA flagged missing traces for a critical payment flow.
- Impact: dashboards show incomplete traces; rollout can still serve traffic but tracing sampling and log correlation broken -> harder to debug downstream failures.

Quick things verified (times in UTC):
- 2025-02-02 22:45: kubectl top nodes OK, node CPU/mem within expected range.
- 2025-02-02 22:50: kafka consumer lag (ingest-log-consumer) increased ~15k messages backlog.
- 2025-02-02 23:05: fluent-bit crashed-and-restarted on node ip-10-0-12-34 (OOMKilled) -> restarted by daemonset.

Commands I ran and raw outputs (snippets):
1) kubectl -n observability logs -l app=fluent-bit --tail=200
> [2025-02-02 23:04:12] [error] Could not parse line as JSON at offset 0: \"TRACE_ID\":  ""
> [2025/02/02 23:04:12] [warn] [input:tail:tail.0] file rotated: /var/log/pods/service-A/*.log
> [2025/02/02 23:04:13] [error] [filter_kube_metadata] Could not get pod info: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = context deadline exceeded

Interpretation: fluent-bit is choking on malformed lines; also kubernetes API calls for metadata are timing out (maybe due to kube-apiserver load or network). Need to correlate with kube-apiserver logs.

2) kubectl -n observability exec -it deploy/jaeger-collector -- curl -s -D - localhost:14268/health | sed -n '1,40p'
> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
> Content-Type: application/json
> {"status":"unavailable","details":"downstream storage: elasticsearch: 503"}

Note: Jaeger reports downstream storage (ES) 503. But our storage recently moved to ClickHouse for traces; double-check collector config. Maybe some instances still point to ES after a partial rollout (see infra PR #412).

3) kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka01:9092 --describe --group ingest-log-consumer
> TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG   CONSUMER-ID
> logs-ingest     0          123456          135678          12222 consumer-1

Action: scaled consumer deployment to 4 replicas -> lag dropped to ~2k. Not a full fix.

4) Prometheus query to check metric series count for service-A latencies
> Query: count({__name__=~"service_a_request_latency_seconds.*"})
> 2025-02-02 23:10 => 12 series
> 2025-02-01 23:10 => 185 series

Hypothesis: label cardinality collapsed (maybe instrumentation changed label names). Check recent deploys for service-A: saw a pull request that renamed route -> endpoint_label. If ingestion pipeline uses label filters, that could drop series.

5) grep raw logs on node (partial)
$ sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep -i "econnrefused"
> Feb 02 23:03:12 ip-10-0-12-34 kubelet[1234]: E090: failed to get pod status: connection refused

So kubelet had transient connection issue to kube-apiserver. Might explain kube metadata filter timing out.

Error snippets collected:
- "Could not parse line as JSON at offset 0: \"TRACE_ID\":  \"\""
- "rpc error: code = Unknown desc = context deadline exceeded" (from filter_kube_metadata)
- "downstream storage: elasticsearch: 503" (jaeger-collector)
- "metric series dropped: 'service_a_request_latency_seconds' - label mismatch" (alerting rule output)
- "kafka: leader not available for partition 2" (from producer logs around 22:40)

Rolling timeline + candidate root causes:
- 21:58: manual infra deploy (infra PR #412) to migrate a small subset of collectors to clickhouse/storage-v2.
- 22:15: network flaps reported on nodes in us-west-2a (cloudwatch Alert ephemeral network).
- 22:30: fluent-bit pod OOM on node ip-10-0-12-34 -> restarted without backoff. During restart, some logs wrote partial/malformed JSON into log files because writer library in service-A was in mid-rotate phase.
- 22:35: kafka leader election churn for partition 2 -> producers get leader-not-available temporarily, writes fail, downstream consumer lags.
- 22:45: jaeger-collector configured to ES still hitting ES cluster that is degraded (503), causing spans not to be accepted; some collectors are on storage-v2 (clickhouse) while others still on ES -> schema mismatch or routing issues.

Primary hypotheses (ranked):
1) Rollout mixture + storage backend mismatch: partial migration left collectors with inconsistent config, causing some spans to be forwarded to ES which is currently degraded. This explains Jaeger 503 and missing traces.
2) Fluent-bit parse+kube metadata failures caused significant fraction of logs/tracing headers to be dropped, breaking trace correlation. Kube API/timeouts + rotated partial lines leads to parse errors.
3) Kafka instability increased backlog -> consumer scaling handled partial backlog but combined with malformed records some messages dropped or skipped.
4) Instrumentation change (label rename) caused Prometheus to collapse series and Alerts to trigger (less likely for tracing drop but explains metric drop).

Immediate mitigations tried and status:
- Scaled ingest-log-consumer to 4 replicas -> backlog reduced but not zero. (status: partial improvement)
- Rolled back the infra PR #412 on staging collectors to restore ES-only behavior -> pending (blocked by infra pipeline approvals).
- Restarted fluent-bit daemonset on affected nodes with updated config to enable strict_json false (to tolerate partial lines) -> fluent-bit logs show reduced parse errors but still see API timeouts. (status: helped parsing)
- Restarted jaeger-collector pod to pick up fresh config -> still 503 until ES cluster health fixed. (status: no change)

Tests to run / next steps (ordered):
- 1) Validate collector config across all replicas: kubectl -n observability get deploy -l app=jaeger-collector -o yaml | grep -E "storage|CLICKHOUSE|ELASTIC" -> ensure uniform backend. Also check ConfigMap used by collectors.
- 2) Check ES cluster health (if still used): curl -s -u es_read:*** https://es-cluster/_cluster/health?level=shards -> record status. If red, coordinate with infra to recover or fail over.
- 3) Force-consume a sample of problematic Kafka messages to inspect payload: kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka01:9092 --topic logs-ingest --partition 2 --offset 123400 --max-messages 50 > sample.json; then run jq -c . on sample.json to see broken JSON lines.
- 4) Run Jaeger query for specific trace id (from payment flow) to see which collector received it: curl -s "http://jaeger-query:16686/api/traces?service=payment-service" | jq '.data | length' -> results currently 0. Cross-check collector logs for that trace id.
- 5) Check kube-apiserver metrics and logs during window 22:00-23:00 for spikes (apiserver request latencies) and correlate with filter_kube_metadata errors.
- 6) Backfill missing series in Prometheus? No — first find instrumentation change in service-A codebase; revert if accidental. Check recent commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-A/commit/7f9c3b.

Notes to file for longer-term fixes:
- Add forwarder-level buffering for fluent-bit to avoid dropping partial JSON during rotation events (debounce file rotation events or use multiline parser with begin/end markers).
- Add a collector-side health-check gating: if downstream storage unavailable, collectors should NACK spans into Kafka for replay rather than silently failing with 503.
- Instrumentation contracts: require backward-compatible label mapping for metrics, and include a migration plan when renaming labels (automated mapping in ingest pipeline).
- Improve runbooks: add a quick checklist for storage-migration rollouts (validate config uniformity before scaling).

Things I still need to do (my mental TODOs):
- [ ] Get infra approval to rollback PR #412 on staging and, if safe, prod. Coordinate with Tom (infra) and Samir (collector owner).
- [ ] Run the kafka-console-consumer sample and attach output to OBS-789 ticket.
- [ ] Add a short telemetry test to CI that verifies traces can be ingested end-to-end (producer -> kafka -> collector -> storage) after infra changes.
- [ ] Follow up with ES team to verify if ES degradation was caused by index-size limits or spike in write QPS.

Slack notes (to copy over into ticket):
- @infra-team saw a partial rollout of collector storage backend at 21:58 that likely left a mixed fleet. Suggest immediate rollback on staging and hold prod.
- @sre increased consumer replicas and restarted fluent-bit; parse errors decreased but Jaeger still 503 -> likely storage issue.

Misc snippets I might later paste into ticket (keep here):
- jaeger-collector log snippet: "ERROR downstream storage: elasticsearch: 503 Service Unavailable - failed to write batch"
- fluent-bit log snippet: "[error] Could not parse line as JSON at offset 0"
- producer log snippet: "kafka: leader not available for partition 2"

If I forget: main suspects = mixed collector configs from infra rollout + transient node/network issues -> parsing + ingestion failures + ES degraded = missing traces. Hypothesis chain: rollout -> node network flap -> kube timeouts -> fluent-bit parse errors -> kafka churn -> consumer lag -> collector writes to degraded ES -> spans lost (503).

If this persists after rollback, next escalate to: infra lead (Tom), storage (es/ch clickhouse) owners, and application owners to quarantine malformed log writers.

End of scratchpad.
